layer_dependence_screen_v2.requirement_4_n_equals_1_is_not_a_licenc: n = 1 IS NOT A LICENCE, AND A SEPARATE EXPLICIT TRACTABILITY JUDGEMENT IS REQUIRED. An argument taking thirty group-traversal steps at ONE interface is not thereby cheap, tractable or in scope -- only not INTERFACE-vacuous. layer_dependence_screen_v2.requirement_5_the_threshold_bounds_the_w: THE ~7 THRESHOLD IS RESTATED AGAINST THE QUANTITY IT ACTUALLY BOUNDS. As written in BATCH-004 it asserted a fact about AVAILABLE CIPHER INTERFACES ('no conversion makes MORE than 7 interfaces available inside RQ-AES-001's 3-7 round scope') and then applied that number to THE ARGUMENT'S ITERATION COUNT. RT-10 demonstrated these are not the same quantity: an argument can iterate arbitrarily many times at one interface, so a bound on the first is not a bound on the second. RESTATEMENT IN FORCE: the ~7 figure bounds THE NUMBER OF CONSECUTIVE SUPER-BOX INTERFACES AVAILABLE INSIDE THE IN-SCOPE ROUND RANGE, and the screen kills a candidate ONLY when THE OBJECT MUST SURVIVE MORE CONSECUTIVE INTERFACES THAN ARE AVAILABLE. It says NOTHING about iteration count at a fixed interface, and it may not be used to kill a candidate on iteration count. AND THE ERROR RUNS IN A KNOWABLE DIRECTION: if residual R5's one-interface-per-round convention is wrong in the direction that a super-box spans TWO rounds, the in-scope budget is 3, not 7, and THE SCREEN IS TOO PERMISSIVE, NOT TOO STRICT. Every candidate is therefore screened under BOTH conversions and the tighter one is reported beside the looser one; advertised margins computed against 7 alone are overstated by more than a factor of two and may not be quoted without the tighter figure.
